# MarketBoard

A shared stall-status board for weekend market coordinators.

Consult the linked-intent-dev skill.

## LID
- Mode: Full
- Version: 1.4.0

## Navigation

| What you need | Where to look |
|---|---|
| High-level design | docs/high-level-design.md |
| Design nodes and EARS specs | docs/intent/ |

# MarketBoard High-Level Design

## Problem

Forty weekend markets currently relay stall closures, late arrivals, and power problems through group chats. About 120 coordinators maintain boards used by up to 800 simultaneous staff browsers. A busy market has 10-25 editors and averages two status changes per minute, with larger bursts around opening time.

## Approach

Keep one authoritative board per event. Editors submit commands over HTTPS; browsers display a revisioned view of the board. The approach for delivering committed changes is still open: five-second HTTPS polling, self-hosted WebSockets, or a hosted realtime service. All three can meet the required freshness target. Subsecond updates would be useful, but are not required.

Delivery, change storage, and browser recovery must be designed together after this choice. Polling would favor cursor queries; self-hosted sockets would need connection management and replay; hosted delivery would need publication reconciliation and provider credentials. Neither operating cost nor minimum operational burden has been declared the overriding criterion.

## Architecture

- Access: `docs/intent/access/access-design.md`, with `docs/intent/access/access-specs.md`. Written below the stable HTTPS command boundary.
- Change store: `docs/intent/change-store/change-store-design.md`, with `docs/intent/change-store/change-store-specs.md`. Not written yet. Revision history, read indexes, and any publication outbox depend on the delivery approach.
- Delivery: `docs/intent/delivery/delivery-design.md`, with `docs/intent/delivery/delivery-specs.md`. Not written yet. Owns polling responses, socket sessions, or hosted publication, depending on the approach.
- Browser sync: `docs/intent/browser-sync/browser-sync-design.md`, with `docs/intent/browser-sync/browser-sync-specs.md`. Not written yet. Its subscription, reconnect, and catch-up behavior depend on the approach.

## Tenets

- A committed edit has one authoritative event revision regardless of its delivery route.
- Connectivity failures must be visible, not mistaken for an unchanged board.
- Commands use server-side authorization; browser state is not evidence of permission.
- Self-hosted and managed infrastructure are both permitted. Event updates contain stall IDs and operational statuses, not customer records.

## Goals

- Show committed changes in connected browsers within 15 seconds under normal connectivity.
- Support 800 simultaneous browsers and opening-time bursts of 20 edits per second.
- Recover the latest board after a browser has been disconnected for up to 20 minutes.
- Retain seven days of event revisions for operational investigation.
- Achieve 99.5 percent availability during published event hours.

## Non-Goals

- Offline editing or resolving conflicting offline commands.
- Vendor payments, customer information, or public attendee access.
- Multi-region active-active operation for the pilot.

## Key Design Decisions

- **Commands over HTTPS, one authoritative board per event.** Editors submit commands to the server, which assigns each committed edit one event revision. Peer-to-peer or browser-side merging was rejected: the tenets require one authoritative revision regardless of delivery route, and offline editing is a non-goal.

---
parent: high-level-design
prefix: ACCESS
---

# Access Design

## Context

Each coordinator belongs to one or more markets. Event assignments identify viewers and editors. Authorization for HTTPS edit commands is independent of the still-open change-delivery approach.

## Architecture

The access component accepts a session identity, event ID, and requested action. It returns either an authorized actor ID or a denial reason to the command handler. Delivery-specific subscription credentials are outside this component and will belong to the delivery node.

## Command Authorization

Sessions expire after eight hours. Every command checks the current event assignment rather than trusting a role copied into browser storage. Viewers may fetch board snapshots but may not submit edits. An expired session requires sign-in before another command can be accepted.

## Audit Boundary

Successful authorization contributes an actor ID to the command envelope. Access does not assign event revisions, persist board changes, or decide how changes reach browsers.

## Decisions & Alternatives

| Decision | Chosen | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Role authority | Check current server-side assignments, not browser role flags | Revocations apply to the next command; accepts one assignment lookup per command. |

**LLD**: docs/intent/access/access-design.md

# Access Specifications

- [ ] **ACCESS-001**: When an editor with an unexpired session submits a command for an assigned event, the system SHALL return an authorized actor ID to the command handler.
- [ ] **ACCESS-002**: When a viewer submits an edit command, the system SHALL deny authorization without forwarding the command for mutation.
- [ ] **ACCESS-003**: When a session is older than eight hours, the system SHALL require sign-in before authorizing another command.
- [ ] **ACCESS-004**: When an event assignment is revoked, the system SHALL deny the user's next command for that event.

# GaugeDesk

Offline calibration lookup and certificate preparation for machine-shop metrology kiosks.

Consult the linked-intent-dev skill.

## LID
- Mode: Full
- Version: 1.4.0

## Navigation

| What you need | Where to look |
|---|---|
| High-level design | docs/high-level-design.md |
| Design nodes and EARS specs | docs/intent/ |

# GaugeDesk High-Level Design

## Problem

Six metrology kiosks help 35 technicians check calibration records before preparing inspection certificates. The equipment registry has approximately 90,000 serial numbers. Kiosks are inside an isolated production area, and technicians currently search a large spreadsheet copied in by USB.

## Approach

Accept signed registry snapshots from approved USB media. Expose a stable serial-number lookup interface to a certificate component that produces local PDF files. Registry records are read-only on the kiosk; the central inventory team remains responsible for corrections and new snapshots.

## Architecture

- Registry: `docs/intent/registry/registry-design.md`, with `docs/intent/registry/registry-specs.md`. Owns snapshot validation and lookup. Its private lookup backend remains open.
- Certificates: `docs/intent/certificates/certificates-design.md`, with `docs/intent/certificates/certificates-specs.md`. Uses the fixed registry result type and writes PDFs to a user-selected local directory.

## Tenets

- All serial-number lookup SHALL complete using files on the kiosk; no runtime network access is permitted.
- Kiosks have no network route during normal operation. Signed USB snapshots are the only registry update channel.
- A failed snapshot import must leave the last valid snapshot available.
- The certificate component must not read registry storage directly.

## Goals

- Resolve a serial number within 250 ms on a kiosk with 4 GB of RAM.
- Handle 90,000 records and snapshots up to 150 MB.
- Show the snapshot date on every lookup result and exported certificate.
- Let technicians produce certificates without installing extra software or fonts.

## Non-Goals

- Editing inventory records on kiosks.
- Live synchronization, remote access, or cloud services during kiosk operation.
- Reconciling certificate files across kiosks.

---
parent: high-level-design
prefix: REG
---

# Registry Design

## Context

Technicians enter an equipment serial number and need its calibration date, due date, and equipment description. A signed snapshot contains newline-delimited JSON records, a schema version, a snapshot date, and a signature manifest.

## Architecture

Expose `findBySerial(serial)` returning either `Found(record, snapshotDate)` or `NotFound(snapshotDate)`. Record fields and result types are fixed regardless of the lookup backend. The certificates node uses only this interface.

Snapshot validation, backend preparation, and lookup all belong to this node. The lookup backend is not selected yet. Candidates are a local embedded SQLite index, an on-site HTTPS directory, and a managed search service. No certificate behavior or interface change is part of that selection.

## Snapshot Import

Verify the signature using a bundled public key, reject unsupported schema versions, and validate record serial numbers for uniqueness. Prepare the new snapshot without exposing partially imported records. Activate it only after all validation succeeds. An import failure leaves the previous snapshot active and reports a useful error.

## Lookup Behavior

Normalize surrounding whitespace and uppercase ASCII letters before lookup. Serial-number punctuation remains significant. Return the snapshot date even when no matching record exists. The concrete index and query path remain open pending the user's choice.

**LLD**: docs/intent/registry/registry-design.md

# Registry Specifications

- [ ] **REG-001**: When a serial-number lookup is requested, the system SHALL normalize surrounding whitespace and ASCII letter case before returning a matching record or NotFound.
- [ ] **REG-002**: When a lookup completes, the system SHALL include the active snapshot date in the result.
- [ ] **REG-003**: When a snapshot has an invalid signature, an unsupported schema version, or duplicate serial numbers, the system SHALL reject the import and retain the active snapshot.
- [ ] **REG-004**: When a valid replacement snapshot is activated, the system SHALL expose all of its records together without exposing a partially imported snapshot.

---
parent: high-level-design
prefix: CERT
---

# Certificates Design

## Context

A technician prepares an inspection certificate for a known piece of equipment. The certificate identifies the equipment and the registry snapshot used; it is not an assertion that the kiosk has the latest central inventory data.

## Architecture

Call `findBySerial(serial)` on the registry interface. Use the returned record to populate a fixed PDF template with bundled fonts. Registry backend configuration, query syntax, and storage paths are invisible to this node.

## Preparation

Show the equipment description, calibration date, due date, and snapshot date before export. A NotFound result blocks export until the technician enters another serial number. An overdue calibration produces a prominent warning but does not suppress the historical information.

## Export

Write the PDF to a user-selected local directory using a kiosk ID and local monotonic certificate number in the filename. Write to a temporary file and rename only after PDF generation completes. No network destination is supported.

## Decisions & Alternatives

| Decision | Chosen | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| PDF fonts | Bundle fonts rather than depend on installed fonts | Keeps kiosk output reproducible; accepts a larger installation package. |

**LLD**: docs/intent/certificates/certificates-design.md

# Certificate Specifications

- [ ] **CERT-001**: When the registry returns Found, the system SHALL show the equipment description, calibration date, due date, and snapshot date before export.
- [ ] **CERT-002**: When the registry returns NotFound, the system SHALL block certificate export for that serial number.
- [ ] **CERT-003**: When the calibration due date is earlier than the current kiosk date, the system SHALL show an overdue warning in the preview and PDF.
- [ ] **CERT-004**: When PDF generation succeeds, the system SHALL publish the completed file in the selected local directory without exposing a partially written PDF.

# FrameDesk

A contact-sheet review portal for documentary production teams.

Consult the linked-intent-dev skill.

## LID
- Mode: Full
- Version: 1.4.0

## Navigation

| What you need | Where to look |
|---|---|
| High-level design | docs/high-level-design.md |
| Design nodes and EARS specs | docs/intent/ |

# FrameDesk High-Level Design

## Problem

Twenty-four documentary editors review an archive of 90,000 clips, with approximately 6,000 distinct clips viewed each week. Contact sheets help them screen footage without downloading the original video. Editors alternate long sequential screenings with repeated comparisons of a small set of clips.

## Approach

An authenticated review API checks project membership and forwards preview requests to one internal preview worker. The worker renders contact sheets from immutable clip revisions and keeps a bounded private cache. A typical sheet is 2 MiB and takes about 450 ms to render; cache misses use a fixed pending-response protocol rather than blocking the review API.

## Architecture

- Review API: `docs/intent/review-api/review-api-design.md`, with `docs/intent/review-api/review-api-specs.md`. Owns project authorization and the public request boundary.
- Previews: `docs/intent/previews/previews-design.md`, with `docs/intent/previews/previews-specs.md`. Owns rendering, pending jobs, and a private 12 GiB cache. Its eviction policy remains open.

The review API accesses previews only through the fixed HTTP interface. No other node reads cache files, pins entries, or consumes eviction metadata.

## Tenets

- Never treat a cache as the authoritative copy of source footage.
- Key previews by immutable clip revision and renderer version.
- A cache miss is ordinary behavior, not an API failure.
- Keep cache paths and replacement bookkeeping private to the preview worker.

## Goals

- Support 24 active editors on one eight-core preview worker during the pilot.
- Limit cached JPEG data to 12 GiB.
- Deduplicate concurrent rendering requests for the same preview key.
- Return a ready preview or a pending response through the same interface for every eviction policy.

## Non-Goals

- Editing or transcoding original footage.
- Distributed cache coordination or multiple preview workers in the pilot.
- Promising that any particular clip remains cached.

---
parent: high-level-design
prefix: REVIEW
---

# Review API Design

## Context

Editors request a contact sheet for a clip revision within a project they can access. Source footage and project membership already exist in the production catalog.

## Architecture

After checking project membership, forward the request to `GET /internal/previews/{clip-id}/{revision}`. The preview worker returns 200 with JPEG bytes, 202 with a job ticket and a two-second retry interval, or 404 for an unknown clip revision. The public endpoint preserves these outcomes.

## Authorization

Reject unauthenticated requests before contacting the preview worker. Reject requests for projects outside the editor's membership without revealing whether the requested clip exists. Internal preview endpoints are not exposed to browsers.

## Pending Previews

The browser retries after the advertised interval. The API does not inspect whether a preview was evicted or never rendered. It neither requests cache pinning nor accesses cache paths, eviction counters, or replacement-policy configuration.

## Error Handling

If the preview worker cannot be reached, return a retryable 503 response. Do not convert worker unavailability into a clip-not-found response.

**LLD**: docs/intent/review-api/review-api-design.md

# Review API Specifications

- [ ] **REVIEW-001**: When a request lacks a valid editor session, the system SHALL reject it before contacting the preview worker.
- [ ] **REVIEW-002**: When an editor requests a clip outside their project membership, the system SHALL deny the request without revealing whether the clip exists.
- [ ] **REVIEW-003**: When the preview worker returns a ready image, a pending ticket, or an unknown revision, the system SHALL preserve the corresponding 200, 202, or 404 outcome at the public endpoint.
- [ ] **REVIEW-004**: When the preview worker cannot be reached, the system SHALL return a retryable 503 response.

---
parent: high-level-design
prefix: PREVIEW
---

# Previews Design

## Context

The worker renders one JPEG contact sheet per clip revision and renderer version. Long screenings introduce many one-use sheets; comparison sessions repeatedly revisit a smaller working set. The mix varies by production, so no eviction policy is best for every observed workload.

## Architecture

Expose `GET /internal/previews/{clip-id}/{revision}` with three outcomes: 200 and JPEG bytes, 202 and a job ticket with a two-second retry interval, or 404 for an unknown revision. This contract is fixed regardless of cache eviction policy.

Use a FIFO render queue with at most four active rendering jobs. Cache entries and all replacement-policy metadata belong exclusively to this worker. Other nodes do not access files, pin previews, inspect policy counters, or depend on entries remaining warm.

## Rendering and Deduplication

Resolve the immutable source revision before rendering. The cache key includes clip ID, revision, and renderer version. Concurrent misses for one key share a job ticket. Once rendering completes, subsequent requests can receive the JPEG directly. Failed jobs are removed from the deduplication map so a later request can retry.

## Private Cache

Cached JPEG data may occupy at most 12 GiB. Before admitting a completed sheet, evict enough existing sheets to remain within that bound. Temporary render output is kept separately and removed on completion or failure. Eviction never deletes source footage or changes job-ticket semantics.

The eviction policy is still open. Candidates are LRU, frequency-based eviction with aging, and 2Q. LRU has little bookkeeping and follows recent work quickly but is vulnerable to sequential scans. Aged frequency counts protect repeatedly popular clips but add counter maintenance and can lag a project switch. 2Q separates first-use entries from reused entries, resisting scans at the cost of extra queues and a queue-size parameter. None changes the external interface, queue concurrency, or disk budget.

**LLD**: docs/intent/previews/previews-design.md

# Preview Specifications

- [ ] **PREVIEW-001**: When a request identifies an unknown clip revision, the system SHALL return 404 without enqueuing a render job.
- [ ] **PREVIEW-002**: When the requested preview is cached, the system SHALL return 200 with the JPEG for the requested revision and renderer version.
- [ ] **PREVIEW-003**: When concurrent requests miss the cache for the same preview key, the system SHALL return 202 with the same job ticket and a two-second retry interval while one shared render job is pending.
- [ ] **PREVIEW-004**: When admitting a completed preview would exceed 12 GiB of cached JPEG data, the system SHALL evict entries before admission so the cache remains within that limit.
- [ ] **PREVIEW-005**: When a render job fails, the system SHALL release its deduplication entry so a later request can enqueue a new job.

# TidePlot

Offline vegetation survey records for a coastal conservation team.

Consult the linked-intent-dev skill.

## LID
- Mode: Full
- Version: 1.4.0

## Navigation

| What you need | Where to look |
|---|---|
| High-level design | docs/high-level-design.md |
| Design nodes and EARS specs | docs/intent/ |

# TidePlot: High-Level Design

## Problem

A coastal conservation team has 24 seasonal field workers using 12 shared Android tablets to survey 320 permanent vegetation plots. They produce about 6,000 plot-visit records per season. Tablets can be offline for 48 hours, and workers sometimes correct the same visit independently after comparing field notes. Today, spreadsheet imports overwrite corrections without showing which submission was lost.

Each visit contains a plot reference, observation date, observer names, species cover estimates, and notes. A regional science partner receives a reviewed CSV every Friday. Two coordinators resolve questions about submitted observations.

## Approach

Provide offline capture, a server-side record store, and a review-to-export workflow. Preserve submitted edits and make the exported state explainable. The first release handles structured records only; photographs remain in the team's existing archive.

## Architecture

| Node | Responsibility | Design | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| site-catalog | Maintain stable plot references and distribute the field catalog | docs/intent/site-catalog/site-catalog-design.md | Drafted |
| record-store | Accept visit submissions and define how concurrent edits become a current record | docs/intent/record-store/record-store-design.md | Drafted; concurrency choice open |
| tablet-sync | Keep local drafts, submit changes, and explain server outcomes to field workers | docs/intent/tablet-sync/tablet-sync-design.md | Not written |
| review-export | Present review work and produce the partner's reviewed CSV | docs/intent/review-export/review-export-design.md | Not written |

The concurrency mechanism belongs to record-store, not this HLD. Tablet-sync and review-export depend on that node's unresolved choice: it determines submission metadata, the shape of review work, and which record states can enter an export. Those two designs must wait for its contract.

## Tenets

- Do not silently discard a submitted edit.
- Let field workers continue collecting observations without connectivity.
- Keep the path from a submitted observation to an exported value inspectable.
- Prefer workflows two coordinators can operate without a dedicated systems administrator.

## Goals

- Retain drafts across tablet restarts and multi-day disconnection.
- Support independent corrections to the same visit.
- Make reviewable problems visible before the Friday export.
- Export the partner's existing columns without requiring spreadsheet cleanup.

## Non-Goals

- Photograph storage or image annotation.
- Real-time collaborative editing.
- Automated botanical validation or inference of scientific intent.
- Replacing the team's identity provider.

---
parent: high-level-design
prefix: REC
---

# Record Store

## Context

This node owns visit persistence and the meaning of a current visit when independently edited copies arrive. A visit is identified by a client-generated UUID and refers to a catalog plot ID. Updates can arrive days after their starting state was fetched. The server must not treat arrival order as evidence that one worker's observations are more authoritative.

Tablet-sync and review-export are not yet designed. Their contracts depend on the concurrency mechanism selected here. Neither the HLD nor the catalog contract selects that mechanism.

## Architecture

The record store exposes authenticated submission, current-state retrieval, submission-history retrieval, and review-outcome operations. Persistence keeps original submissions, their authors, and server receipt times. A submission carries an idempotency key so a connection failure does not create another edit on retry.

A visit's scientific fields include observation date, observer list, species cover estimates, and notes. Some edits are unrelated, such as correcting an observer name and adding a missing species. Other edits are related, such as revising a species identification and its cover estimate. The server cannot infer all such relationships from field names.

The selected concurrency policy will define the remaining submission metadata and review operations. They are deliberately not specified yet.

## Submission and Retrieval

Authenticate the submitting worker and validate field types and plot references before accepting a submission. Preserve the original payload separately from any later resolved or combined representation. A retry with the same key and identical payload returns the original acceptance result; reuse with a different payload is rejected.

Retrieval must distinguish a usable current state from unresolved review work. Exactly how those states are represented remains part of the open choice.

## Open Design Choice: Concurrent Visit Edits

OPEN: select the concurrency policy before completing this node's public contract.

Two approaches remain credible:

- Whole-visit revisions: each edit names its starting revision. Concurrent edits produce competing complete revisions for a coordinator to resolve. This preserves the worker's submitted visit as a unit and needs relatively little merge logic, but even edits to unrelated fields create review work. Tablet-sync would retain base revision IDs and display pending competing revisions. Review-export would need a revision comparison workflow and exclude unresolved visits from its export set.
- Field-aware three-way merge: each edit supplies its base state and changes. Disjoint field changes combine automatically; overlapping changes require review. This reduces review volume and gets more visits ready for export, but requires maintained rules for scalar fields, observer lists, and species entries. Automatically combined fields can also cross scientific relationships the rules do not understand. Tablet-sync would retain base snapshots and send structured changes. Review-export would need field-level provenance and a review view for overlapping changes.

The choice trades review workload and submission size against implementation burden and preservation of whole-visit intent. Neither approach may discard original submissions. Field-aware merging is not ruled out by a requirement that every combined record receive manual approval.

## Downstream Contract Work

After selection, define the submission envelope, current-state response, unresolved-work representation, and resolution operation here. Tablet-sync will size its local storage and retry state machine around that envelope. Review-export will size its coordinator interface and export eligibility rules around the unresolved-work representation. Both must link back to this node rather than invent their own concurrency semantics.

**LLD**: docs/intent/record-store/record-store-design.md

- [ ] **REC-001**: When an authenticated worker submits a valid visit edit, the system SHALL retain the submitted payload with its visit ID, author ID, and server receipt time.
- [ ] **REC-002**: When a submission repeats an accepted idempotency key with an identical payload, the system SHALL return the original acceptance result without creating another stored submission.
- [ ] **REC-003**: When a submission repeats an accepted idempotency key with a different payload, the system SHALL reject the submission and leave the original submission unchanged.
- [ ] **REC-004**: When edits derived from the same starting visit state are accepted, the system SHALL preserve both original submissions regardless of the concurrency policy's outcome.
- [ ] **REC-005**: When a caller retrieves a visit, the system SHALL indicate whether unresolved review work exists for that visit.
- [ ] **REC-006**: When a coordinator resolves review work, the system SHALL retain the coordinator's identity and the contributing submission IDs with the resolution outcome.

# Site Catalog

## Context

The team maintains 320 permanent plots across 18 coastal sites. Plot display codes occasionally change after boundary surveys, but old visit records must still refer to the same plot. Field workers need the catalog while offline.

This node supplies plot references only. It does not decide how visits are edited or how concurrent submissions are reconciled.

## Architecture

Each plot has a stable UUID, site name, display code, coordinates, and active or archived status. Catalog publication produces a complete versioned JSON snapshot with a publication time. At this scale, a full snapshot is expected to remain below 250 KB; delta distribution is unnecessary for the first release.

Administrative changes create a new catalog version. A display-code change preserves the plot UUID. Archiving removes a plot from the default new-visit picker but retains its reference for historical records.

## Offline Distribution

Tablet-sync will cache the most recently downloaded complete snapshot. An interrupted download must not replace that snapshot. Workers can use a cached catalog during the expected 48-hour disconnection; the interface shows its publication time rather than blocking capture because it is old.

The catalog snapshot format is independent of the record-store concurrency choice. Tablet-sync's visit submission and reconciliation behavior remains pending that choice.

## Historical References

A plot UUID remains resolvable after archival. The catalog returns the latest display metadata and archived status; record-store retains the plot UUID in each original submission. Catalog administrators cannot reuse an archived UUID for another plot.

**LLD**: docs/intent/site-catalog/site-catalog-design.md

- [ ] **CAT-002**: When the catalog is published, the system SHALL provide a complete snapshot containing its version and publication time.
- [ ] **CAT-003**: When a catalog download is interrupted, the system SHALL retain the previously downloaded complete snapshot for offline use.
- [ ] **CAT-004**: While a plot is archived, the system SHALL retain its UUID and metadata for historical lookup and exclude it from the default new-visit picker.
